paragraphs.source_en: Dokusen, with an air of solemn mystery, said, “The upward path cannot be opened up by means of a violin. If one could grasp the truth of the universe in such a spirit of playful absorption, that would be a serious matter indeed. If you wish to know the inner meaning of it, you must let go from the cliff; without the spirit to revive after absolute death, it will never do.” It was all very well for him to deliver this sermon-like admonition to Tofu, but Tofu was a man who did not know even the first syllable of Zen Buddhism, so he showed not the slightest sign of being impressed. He said, “Well! That may be so, but I believe art expresses the highest ideal for which human life thirsts, and in any case it must not be cast aside.”
